关于打印问题的一些解答：
1.测试使用的耗材为白色PLA Basic,我看了评论区有很多朋友肋骨或者脚骨处打印出现了偏移，这通常是散热不足导致的层间粘合问题，打印本模型建议全程打开仓门散热，如果仓外温度＞37℃的地区，建议外墙速度降至80mm/s以下。
2.关于骨骼不跳舞的原因：原因a：检查中轴固定的耗材丝是否平直，扭曲会造成卡顿；原因b：出气的速率要控制在3.5L/min左右，在刚开始的过程中可以手动倾斜一个角度让它形成稳定的气泡后放开手；原因C：请保证底座处于水平状态，倾斜会持续造成模型卡在某一节点；原因D:有少部分模型可能存在版本问题，建议检查一下骨骼站立的盖子是否属于最新的版本。

 

7.27    1时 修正了固定槽公差太紧和脚固定位置偏外的问题，如果脚还是太宽，可以自己调一下卡槽两个预留方块的间隙。

7.26  10时 添加了骨架和底座固定槽及优化了打印参数

7.25  16时 修正了一些参数及模型问题

🐟 一口气泵，骨架就跳起来了。
装在鱼缸里的"打氧跳舞摆件"：气泵的气泡/气流从气管进入主体，顶动内部斜放的挡板，让盒体来回轻摆——站在上面的可动小骨架就跟着"跳舞"。好玩、解压，还能给水面添点动静。

✨ 本版亮点：底部吸盘 + 全程免支撑

  • 吸盘在底部：安装柱竖直朝下，贴缸底/缸壁更稳，不易被水流冲歪。
  • 打印无需支撑：吸盘柱竖向、悬垂面已优化，可关掉支撑直接打——省料、省时、表面干净、没拆支撑的疤，新手友好。

  • 已实测：已打印并通气测试，骨架摆动正常、吸盘固定牢靠。

    吸盘尺寸：

🧩 兼容与玩法

  • 顶部兼容任意关节可动骨架/小人，自行用胶水定 pose。
  • 主体与挡板分件打印；中间固定孔穿一段打印耗材丝，两端烫平/压扁当销（兼作铰链），把挡板连成可摆结构。

🔧 装配 4 步

 

1.打印主体（含底部吸盘柱）与挡板。

2.取一小段耗材丝穿过中间固定孔，两端用烙铁/打火机烫平（或剪断卡紧）当销/铰链；确认挡板能自由摆动。

3.骨架站上去，胶水固定关节。

4.底部装入蘑菇头吸盘/石头固定支架 → 吸到缸底/缸壁 → 接气管 → 开气泵，开跳 💃

📐 适配吸盘规格（配件实测值，已填好）

  • 型号：2.5 cm 蘑菇平头吸盘
  • 吸盘面外径：25 mm
  • 蘑菇头（平帽）直径：7.5 mm
  • 卡颈高度：2 mm
  • 卡颈直径：4 mm
  • 匹配打印孔（建议，请按你模型实际孔确认）：通孔 ≈ 4.0–4.2 mm 卡住 4 mm 颈；该处板厚 ≈ 2 mm 贴合颈高夹紧；帽侧留 ≥ 8 mm 沉孔/让位，让 7.5 mm 平头贴平。
  • 气管内径：约【4.7 mm】（如你的孔不同请改）

🖨️ 打印建议（实测配方 · 重点：不用支撑）

  • 层高 0.12 mm（实测配方；赶时间可 0.16 / 0.2 草稿）
  • 壁厚 2–3 圈 ｜ 填充 15–20%
  • 支撑：关闭 ✅
  • 摆放：吸盘柱朝下贴板；挡板单独平放
  • 底板附着：Brim 5 mm（实测推荐，保住吸盘柱细脚的首层附着）
  • 接缝：背面或随机
  • 耗材：浸水/有加热灯的缸建议 PETG；PLA 仅短期展示，泡水+升温易软化变形。能控翘边也可 ASA/ABS。

Dancing Skeleton Aquarium Aeration Ornament | Support-Free Optimized Version

Some answers regarding printing issues:
1. The filament used for testing was white PLA Basic. I've seen many comments from friends experiencing shifts in the ribs or foot bones during printing. This is usually a layer adhesion issue caused by insufficient cooling. When printing this model, it is recommended to keep the chamber door open for cooling throughout the entire print. If the ambient temperature is >37℃, it's recommended to reduce the outer wall speed to below 80mm/s.
2. Reasons why the skeleton might not dance: a: Check if the filament string used for the central axis is straight; twisting can cause jamming. b: The air output rate should be controlled at around 3.5 L/min. Initially, you can manually tilt it to form stable bubbles before releasing it. C: Please ensure the base is level; tilting will continuously cause the model to get stuck at a certain point. D: A small number of models might have version issues; it's recommended to check if the lid where the skeleton stands is the latest version.

 

7.27 1 AM: Fixed issues with the mounting groove tolerance being too tight and the foot mounting position being too far outward. If the feet are still too wide, you can adjust the gap between the two reserved squares in the slot yourself.

7.26 10 AM: Added skeleton and base mounting grooves and optimized printing parameters.

7.25 4 PM: Corrected some parameters and model issues.

🐟 One air pump, and the skeleton starts to dance.
The "aerating dancing ornament" in the fish tank: the air pump's bubbles/airflow enter the main body through the air tube, pushing the internal, diagonally placed **baffle**, causing the box to sway back and forth—and the movable little skeleton standing on it starts to "dance." It's fun, stress-relieving, and adds some activity to the water surface.

✨ This version's highlights: Bottom suction cup + Support-free throughout

  • Suction cup at the bottom: The mounting post points vertically downwards, making it more stable when attached to the tank bottom/wall, less likely to be dislodged by water flow.
  • No supports needed for printing: The suction cup post is vertical, and overhangs have been optimized, allowing you to **turn off supports** and print directly—saving material, time, ensuring a clean surface without support removal marks, and being beginner-friendly.

  • Tested: Printed and aeration tested, skeleton movement is normal, suction cup is securely fixed.

    Suction cup dimensions:

🧩 Compatibility and Playability

  • The top is compatible with **any articulated skeleton/figure**; use glue to set its pose.
  • The main body and baffle are printed as separate parts; **thread a piece of filament through the central mounting hole**, flatten/press down both ends to act as pins (also serving as hinges), connecting the baffle into a movable structure.

🔧 Assembly in 4 steps

 

1. Print the main body (including the bottom suction cup post) and the baffle.

2. Thread a small piece of filament through the **central mounting hole**, flatten (or cut and secure tightly) both ends with a soldering iron/lighter to act as pins/hinges; ensure the baffle can swing freely.

3. Place the skeleton on top, fix the joints with glue.

4. Install a mushroom-head suction cup/stone fixing bracket at the bottom → Attach to the tank bottom/wall → Connect the air tube → Turn on the air pump, let it dance 💃

📐 Compatible Suction Cup Specifications (Accessory measured values, already filled)

  • Model: 2.5 cm mushroom **flat-head** suction cup
  • Suction cup face outer diameter: 25 mm
  • Mushroom head (flat cap) diameter: 7.5 mm
  • Neck height: 2 mm
  • Neck diameter: 4 mm
  • Matching print hole (recommendation, **please confirm based on your actual model's hole**): Through-hole ≈ 4.0–4.2 mm to hold the 4 mm neck; plate thickness at this point ≈ 2 mm to tightly fit the neck height; leave ≥ 8 mm counterbore/clearance on the cap side for the 7.5 mm flat head to sit flush.
  • Air tube inner diameter: approximately [4.7 mm] (please change if your hole is different)

🖨️ Printing Recommendations (Tested recipe · Key point: No supports)

  • Layer height **0.12 mm** (tested recipe; for quick prints, use 0.16 / 0.2 draft)
  • Walls 2–3 loops ｜ Infill 15–20%
  • Supports: Off ✅
  • Orientation: Suction cup post **facing down on the plate**; baffle placed flat separately
  • Build plate adhesion: **Brim 5 mm** (tested recommendation to secure the first layer adhesion of the thin suction cup post)
  • Seam: Back or random
  • Filament: For tanks with submerged elements/heating lamps, PETG is recommended; PLA is only for short-term display, as soaking in water + rising temperatures can easily soften and deform it. If warping can be controlled, ASA/ABS can also be used.

instances.summary:

2. Wall Generator changed to Arachne The skeleton is composed of incredibly delicate, tapering details such as the thin ribs, tiny fingers, and intricate joint hinges. The Arachne engine dynamically adjusts the extrusion line width to perfectly trace these narrow, variable-width features,

4. Initial Layer Speed reduced to 35 mm/s 

5. Top Shell Layers reduced to 4 

6. Smooth Coefficient increased to 140 This minimizes mechanical vibrations, resulting in cleaner perimeters and much more accurate tolerances for the moving joints.

json.title: Parametric Electronics Panel Generator - OpenSCAD
json.summary:
Boost MeThank You :)

Parametric Electronics Panel Generator

Create fully customized front panels for electronics projects directly in MakerWorld’s Parametric Model Maker.

This generator combines a configurable base plate, component-specific cutout presets, fan openings, mounting holes and optional labels in one single OpenSCAD file. It is designed for control panels, power supplies, workshop equipment, enclosures, test stations, model-making projects and other custom electronics applications.

Customizable panel

The base panel can be adjusted to fit the required enclosure or installation area.

Available panel settings include:

  • panel width and height
  • panel thickness
  • rounded corners
  • upper edge chamfer
  • optional raised border
  • four optional mounting holes
  • optional countersinks
  • manual or automatic cutout arrangement

The model is centered around the origin and has a completely flat underside for easy printing.

Up to 10 configurable cutouts

The panel supports up to ten independently configurable component positions.

Each cutout can be:

  • enabled or disabled
  • positioned individually
  • rotated freely
  • arranged automatically in a grid
  • combined with mounting holes
  • combined with anti-rotation holes
  • combined with side locking reliefs
  • labeled separately

Selecting None disables the corresponding cutout.

Included cutout types

The generator includes basic geometric openings as well as presets for common electronic components.

Available types include:

  • round hole
  • slot
  • rectangle
  • rounded rectangle
  • USB-A
  • USB-C
  • RJ45
  • toggle switch
  • rocker switch
  • potentiometer
  • rotary encoder
  • display
  • standard fan sizes
  • custom fan

The component presets use different starting geometries and optional secondary openings. Manual dimensions can still be used when a specific component differs from the preset.

Because component dimensions vary between manufacturers, the actual part should always be measured before printing the final panel.

Fan cutouts and ventilation grills

Fan cutouts include the central airflow area and the corresponding mounting-hole pattern.

Available fan options include several standard sizes and a fully customizable fan type.

Different ventilation styles can be selected:

  • open circle
  • cross
  • radial slots
  • honeycomb
  • concentric rings

The grill rotation, bar width, opening size and mounting-hole dimensions can be adjusted.

Individual component labels

Every cutout can receive its own text label.

For each label, the following can be configured:

  • label text
  • engraved or raised style
  • position above, below, left or right
  • text size
  • text depth or height
  • distance from the component
  • additional X and Y offset
  • independent text rotation

The label is positioned relative to the associated component and moves together with it when the cutout is repositioned.

Typical labels include:

POWER USB NETWORK DISPLAY FAN INPUT OUTPUT RESET VOLUME ON / OFF

 

All component labels can also be disabled globally.

Optional panel title

A separate title can be added to the complete panel.

The title can be placed at the top or bottom and can be either engraved or raised.

Possible applications include:

CONTROL PANEL POWER SUPPLY FAN CONTROLLER TEST STATION WORKSHOP CONTROL BATTERY MONITOR

 

The title size, depth, edge distance, position and rotation can be adjusted independently.

Automatic layout

When automatic layout is enabled, all active cutouts are placed in a configurable grid.

The user can define:

  • number of columns
  • horizontal spacing
  • vertical spacing
  • complete layout offset

Individual cutout dimensions and rotations remain active, while their manual position values are ignored.

Typical applications

The generator is suitable for:

  • electronics enclosures
  • control panels
  • bench power supplies
  • workshop machines
  • fan controllers
  • test equipment
  • Raspberry Pi and microcontroller projects
  • audio equipment
  • vehicle and camper installations
  • robotics and model making
  • custom switch and connector panels

Printing

The panel is designed to print with its flat rear side directly on the build plate.

In this orientation:

  • the chamfer faces upward
  • countersinks face upward
  • engraved labels remain visible
  • raised labels are printed on top
  • supports are normally not required

For mechanically loaded panels, use a suitable material and sufficient wall thickness.

Important note

The included presets are intended as practical starting points. USB modules, RJ45 sockets, switches, displays and other components are not fully standardized between manufacturers.

Always measure the actual component and verify:

  • main opening dimensions
  • mounting-hole spacing
  • locking tabs
  • panel thickness requirements
  • required printing tolerance

V2 includes XT60!

json.title: HVAC & Radiator Fin Straightener Comb
json.summary:
🛠️ Universal HVAC & Radiator Fin Straightener Comb

An essential workshop and maintenance tool for air conditioners, radiators, and finned-pack heat exchangers. This tool allows you to precisely straighten bent or crushed aluminum fins, restoring proper airflow and heat exchange efficiency.

Designed to be modular, customizable, and durable: the comb heads are interchangeable via a printed thumb screw to quickly swap between different fin pitches.

📐 Included Fin Pitches (6 Print Plates)

The comb file includes 6 separate print plates, each clearly embossed with its corresponding fin pitch size:

  • 1.6 mm pitch
  • 1.8 mm pitch
  • 2.1 mm pitch
  • 2.3 mm pitch
  • 2.5 mm pitch
  • 3.2 mm pitch

🧵 Material Recommendations (IMPORTANT)

For maximum durability and functionality, use two different materials:

  1. HANDLE ➔ PETG:
    • PETG provides the ideal mechanical strength and flexibility required for the handle to absorb bending stress while pulling across the fin pack.
  2. COMB HEADS & SCREW ➔ PLA:
    • Do NOT print the comb heads in PETG! PETG teeth are too soft and flexible to straighten aluminum. PLA offers the necessary stiffness and hardness for the teeth to push through bent aluminum fins without flexing.

⚙️ Recommended Print Settings

🟡 File 1: Handle (PETG)

  • Layer Height: 0.20 mm
  • Wall Loops: 5
  • Top/Bottom Shells: 5 layers
  • Infill: 20% Gyroid
  • Supports: Yes

⚪ File 2: Comb Heads & Screw (PLA)

  • Layer Height: 0.20 mm
  • Wall Loops: 3
  • Top Shells: 3 layers / Bottom Shells: 4 layers
  • Infill: 15% Gyroid
  • Supports: None required

🔧 Assembly

  1. Select the comb head matching your heat exchanger's fin pitch.
  2. Insert the head into the handle slot.
  3. Hand-tighten the PLA thumb screw until secure. No extra metal hardware needed!

Rugged Screw Unit XL Collection - (Gridfinity Stackable)

 

 CUSTOM LABEL GENERATOR - Click Customize for Small & Wide (BETA)

 

 

 

 

 

What's Special about the Rugged Screw Unit?

  • Added drawer stops!!! Don't accidentally spill your screws.
  • Gridfinity for easy stack-ability
  • Scoop drawers
  • Large Screw holes for wall mounting.
  • Compatible with all Rugged Organizer drawers 
  • 6x2 magnets with glue. Glue in hole(s)

PRINT SETTINGS:

  • Layer Height: 0.2mm
  • DRAWERS: Supports Recommended (Normal Supports on front lip ONLY)
  • I setup the Frame to print vertically (backside down) without supports. There was a little stringing under some of the gridfinity, but that did not warrant me using supports. 10 seconds of post processing (just clip the saging strings) saves a lot of print time. If you want or need to use supports, I'd recommend paint on manual supports only under each grid finity block on the bottom.
  • Build Plate: Large prints like this are prone to warping. I recommend using GLUE / Nano Polymer on your build plate, and lower the AUX fan speed to 20-50% prevent warping!

 

Q&A - What does Gridfinity 4x6, 2x5, 3x4, 2x5, etc. mean?

1. Initial Layer Speed reduced to 35 mm/s 

2. Wall Generator changed to Arachne The Arachne engine dynamically adjusts the extrusion line width to flawlessly fill these narrow, variable-width geometries

5. Top Z Distance increased to 0.26 mm  Increasing the top interface gap from the default 0.2 mm to 0.26 mm ensures that the supports break away effortlessly, preventing ugly stress whitening or rough scarring on the delicate underside of the wireframe.

json.title: Wearable Articulated Finger Extension
json.summary:
Assembly Demonstration

Maker’s Note

I’m a hobby modeler, and I'm trying to enter MakerWorld contests with designs that push me beyond my limits. This is my biggest project so far, and it took many weekends of modeling, printing, testing, breaking parts, and going back to the drawing board. (I have an ever increasing pile of failed prototypes)

My long-term goal is to create a free, easy-to-print and easy-to-assemble parametric generator that lets anyone generate a set of toy fingers fitted to their own hand.

I do have a slight tendency toward maximalism, so I’m not ready to publish the fully customizable version until I’ve confirmed that it works reliably across a wide range of finger sizes, but in the meantime, I wanted to see how people react to the idea and whether it is worth putting the extra work into the generator.

Please try the current version with an open mind, and feel free to leave constructive feedback. I’ll do my best to incorporate the feedback into the customizable version.

 

Background

I first came across this type of finger extension in this Adam Savage video. It immediately looked like something that would be incredibly fun to build and wear… Then I looked at the price tag :D (after spending so much time on this, I fully understand the pricing. Gary's fingers are truly a work of art both aesthetically and mechanically)

That sent me down the rabbit hole of researching how I could make my own. While looking through existing projects and mechanisms, I found the work of Dragonator, whose notes were invaluable during the development process.

A big shoutout to him. Seeing his amazing model, I’m sure he is one of the few who understand both the pain of designing a mechanism like this and the joy of finally putting it on for the first time and feeling the fingers move with your hand.

 

Design Considerations

I’ll demonstrate the main design decisions with pictures below, but these were the areas I focused on most:

Cylindrical, adaptive geometry

The mechanism is built around mostly cylindrical finger sections. This makes a final design I find aesthetic. I believe most similar finger have an adaptable base section that goes around the fingers, and the rest of the mechanism is interchangeable. I wanted the whole finger to be driven by parameters.

Low-profile control shaft movement

One thing I struggled a lot with is how to keep the controller shaft as low to the body as possible both at the two end states, and during the movement.

With a few tradeoffs, I think I well achieved both.

Easy assembly

This was the thing I feared the most. In the commercial version, there is obviously no assembly required, it is put together beautifully with additional hardware. I tried different ways of connecting parts, and after multiple failures came up with a snap-in design, which I'm truly proud of.

Clean seam lines

I wanted the finger to have a clean, cylindrical look when it's straight. However cylinders generally have problems with seam lines. I intentionally placed a straight groove at the bottom of the parts, so you wont need to paint seam lines yourself, you can just hit print and know the lines will look acceptable.

The support tradeoff

This is the price I decided to pay. Many things in my design are supported, and while many I could have eliminated, I decided the one-time price of removing the supports is well covered by the gains I got in aesthetics and assembly.

 

How the Mechanism Works

The finger sections are linked together so that movement from your real finger is transferred through the control shafts to the extended segments.

The animation below shows the movement more clearly than I could explain it in text.

Personal use only. This version has my watermark. For the version without the watermark, it must be purchased on my website.

 

✨ No AMS needed!

All sizes included.
- 12oz standard soda can & 16oz
- 12oz slim, 8.4oz slim, 7.5oz mini, and 8.4oz Alani
 

There are 2 different size pumpkins. The Slim size is smaller than the Standard.

 

The slim size pumpkin (holding in listing photo) has 4 inserts for 12oz slim, 8.4oz slim, 7.5oz mini, and 8.4oz Alani cans.

The larger size has inserts for 12oz standard and 16oz cans.

All insert sizes are labeled in the 3MF and each STL is labeled. Please make sure you print the correct size.

I simply write the size on the bottom of the printed insert with a silver sharpie. 

By request, I have added a version without eyelashes. This version uses the same face as the top, but I do have plans to add different faces. 

Support Removal:

  • I do not recommend trying to pull the supports out from the front with pliers. 
  • It is easier to push the supports through.
  • I personally use a pick and a small hammer and tap the supports through. It does not require a lot of force or effort. 
  • If you are using the version with eyelashes, it is a bit more difficult to remove suppports. I use and x-acto knife to get the supports out from between the eyelashes. 
  • Make sure to remove supports from behind the eyelashes on the inside or the insert will not go all the way in.

Important:

This design requires the use of supports and requires you to know how to tweak your support settings for the cleanest print. I do not offer support outside of errors with the file. This file has been test printed a lot and is fully functional and without errors. 

 

  • if you get stringing, adjust your supports or research the best settings for your printer and filament.
  • I use Bambu Basic PLA Pumpkin Orange and Basic PLA Black for this design.
  • I have not tested with Matte filaments. This could cause the insert to be harder to insert and remove.

json.summary:
Catch the sleepiest Pokémon in its most active form with this adorable Snorlax Roly-Poly Toy! 💤

Designed as a self-righting wobble toy, this sleepy giant tumbles, rocks, and spins for a delightfully long time before rolling right back up again. This model combines real physics with playful interaction, creating a fun, hands-on experience for all ages while encouraging curiosity and exploration!

⚙️ Technical Features & Design

Built to be an elegant, easy-to-print project, this model maximizes performance while remaining incredibly user-friendly:

  • Physics-based Balance: The geometry and center of mass were meticulously optimized using advanced physics simulations, resulting in the longest and smoothest wobbles yet!
  • NO AMS Needed: A smart multipart design lets you print all parts separately, before assembling them in 6 simple steps.

json.title: Android 21 Realistic Multi-Color Parted Statue
json.summary:
Android 21 (Evil) Realistic Multi-Color Parted Statue

 

1. Concept & Design

This statue reimagines Android 21 (Majin form) with a realistic anatomical style while preserving her iconic dangerous aura and allure. The physique is intentionally stylized—finely detailed abdominal muscles, tense dynamic limbs, and a confident forward-leaning battle stance—amplifying the intimidating elegance behind her character.

Engineered as a fully multi-color parted model, every major visual element is physically separated: her volumetric silver-gray hair, black tube top, gold arm rings, gloves, boots, belt, baggy pants, face features, and even her long pink tail. Each color exists as an individual printed part, meaning no AMS, no filament swapping required, yet the final assembly achieves a near-collectible finish straight off the print bed.

2. Engineering & Recommended Assembly Order

The model is engineered to significantly reduce print time and failure risk. All parts are intentionally designed with forgiving tolerances. Since printers often vary slightly in dimensional accuracy, each part is meant to be joined securely using CA glue (super glue).

Gently heating joint areas with a heat gun before applying glue helps the adhesive cure faster and bond stronger.

⚠️ CRITICAL ASSEMBLY STEPS & PRO TIPS:

To avoid top-heavy balance issues during gluing, please follow this precise assembly sequence:

  1. Upper Torso (Important Note):
    • Assemble the upper chest and shoulders first, and then attach the black tube top clothing piece. This ensures a smooth fit and seamless alignment.
  2. Head & Hair Module:
    • Combine the main volumetric hair and face piece first. Next, attach the neck and front bangs, and finally mount the complete head assembly onto the upper torso.
  3. Lower Body & Tail:
    • Pre-assemble the pants, boots, and belt completely, then attach the pink tail.
  4. Final Upper-to-Lower Merge (Pro Tip):
    • Complete the lower body group (pants + boots + belt + tail) first before joining it with the upper body. Installing top parts too early creates heavy top-weight from the massive hair, making lower joint gluing extremely difficult and forcing awkward holding angles while waiting for glue to set!

3. Display & Customization

Although fully colored through part separation alone, painters may optionally enhance shadows on the black top, gold trims, or skin folds to further elevate realism. Her fierce stance and striking silhouette make this statue ideal as a standalone centerpiece or as part of a paired display alongside Majin Buu.

The clean part boundaries also make it enjoyable for hobbyists who prefer hybrid finishing—mixing raw printed colors with light airbrush detailing.

4. Conclusion

Following the release of Majin Buu, this Android 21 statue marks another exciting milestone in multi-color parted sculpture design. It delivers an accessible printing experience while maintaining professional visual depth. Your support and patience made this milestone possible, and more multi-color parted designs are actively in development.

Quick Tips:

  • For complex prints, avoid photography mode: It increases carriage travel and print failure risks.
  • Calibrate your machine and use dry, stable filament to maximize printing reliability.
  • Filament preference: Bambu’s gray remains my personal favorite.
  • Cleanup tools: Needle-nose pliers and Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper make support removal significantly easier.

json.title: Life Size Xenomorph Alien Model - 5ft Tall!
json.titleTranslated: Life Size Xenomorph Alien Model - 5ft Tall!
json.summary:
Large Xenomorph!

 

The time if finally here to post a project I have been working on over the last month. After the recent set of my smaller Xenomorph models, I got peer-pressured into making one that was lifesized (ish). 

 

This model model stands 5ft tall from floor to tip of tail, measures almost 6ft long diagonally from the back foot to the tip of the head, and is almost 4 foot wide! In order to get it to fit through my doorways I ended up leaving the Head, Right Arm, and half othe tail removable and not fully glued in place. 

 

This project is not for everyone and requires quite a bit of dedication and printing resouces to make. At the time of the upload I only sliced the model to fit the H series and A2L printers (to maximize the the size of pieces I could print). Please note that if you are changing your printer from the current H2D that is seleted in the profile you may need to move some pieces around to make sure they fully fit within the build volume. Most are OK, but some have next to no wiggle room for placement. Please also note that the current profile is set to be printed with a .6mm nozzle. This helps speed up print time and the use the .3x layer heights* 

 

 

I printed my model with a very low infill amount (3-4% for most of the print) with the exception of some of the support/critical stress pieces where I increased  the infill. This allowed to print quick and not use too much filament. I printed my model in MATTE PLA from Bambu, but due to the low infill amount, and the size/geometry of the model I REALLY wish I did it PETG so that I could display it outside and not worry about the tail melting/bending in the sun (still a risk with PETG I guess, but not as much). 

 

The assembly requires and advaced level of skill, this is not for first time large model printers. I did my best to make hexagonal pegs to help align everything, but you will likely need to sand all of the surfaces to ensure a good fit. I used CA glue on the pegs, with a 2-part expoxy to hold the flat surfaces together. To fill the joints I useda 2-part epoxy putty that I found on Amazon. Please note that the Base Tail section and the main body has an interference that I didn't catch until after the model was fully sliced and will need to be manually trimmed/sanded when doing the test fitting. I just used my scraper and knife to snip away bits of the main body until the tail section could fully fit. Please be careful test fitting pieces, due to the low infill amount it can be easy to break*** 

 

 

After the resin cured and the gaps were filled I sanded the joints using 320 grit sand paper before applying a bit of primer, and I used a Gloss Black spray paint to the the entire model. I ended up using a total of 6 spray paint cans* so plan accordingly. 
 

 

The Drool was accomplished using a 2-part epoxy resin (for fiberglass in my particular case) and I used some 2" brushes to coat the entire model and make it appear more wet than the gloss paint achieved by itself. To get the drool effect, I waited until the resin was just about dried, and kept applying over the mouth area until it didn't fully run off. A good/easier way to do this may be with some UV activated epoxy that cures in 5-10 seconds, but I have not tried this route. The teeth were painted in steps between the epoxy using an air brush.
